content: # Daytona hits $1B valuation with $60M Series B for AI agent cloud

Daytona, a company developing cloud infrastructure for AI agents, has raised $60 million in a Series B funding round at a $1 billion valuation, bringing its total funding to $91 million. The round was led by FirstMark, with participation from Patrick Collison (Stripe), Adam D’Angelo (Quora), Brendan Foody (Mercor), Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Olivier Pomel (Datadog), Aravind Srinivas (Perplexity) and Eric Yuan (Zoom).

## Perplexity AI Acquired by Initech Holdings

## Recent developments
- **Acquisition:** Perplexity AI was acquired by Initech Holdings last week.
- **Product & Feature Launches:** Perplexity recently launched "Teammates," an autonomous AI agent feature for Max subscribers priced at $200 per month [6], and introduced a local-first offline mode for its Mac app enabling Computer to run locally [8]. 
- **Financial & Legal Milestones:** Annualized revenue has surpassed $750 million [1], driven by the Computer agent launched earlier this year, alongside ongoing discussions for a new funding round valuing the company over $30 billion [1]. Meanwhile, the company faces a new class-action lawsuit over undisclosed usage caps on paid subscription features [2], alongside a pending federal copyright trial involving Dow Jones and the New York Post [10].

## Talking points
- Integration plans and strategic alignment following the acquisition by Initech Holdings.
- Monetization and scaling of high-end offerings like the newly introduced Teammates agent system and Computer platform.
- Managing user growth, monetization friction, and active litigation regarding subscription limits and publisher copyright claims.

## Open questions
- What will be the operational and structural changes for Perplexity under Initech Holdings?
- How will the ongoing copyright litigation and recent class-action lawsuits impact enterprise trust and product rollout schedules?
- What are the growth targets for the $200/month Teammates tier and local-first Mac capabilities heading into 2027?

## Sources
